findings.issue_text: Google Calendar persists the Zod safeParse envelope as the credential key: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the full { success, data } envelope but googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts assigns it directly to key and writes it to the DB, so after any routine token refresh key.access_token and key.refresh_token are undefined and every Google Calendar operation and all future refreshes fail permanently for that user

minimumTokenResponseSchema's computed key [z.string().toString()] evaluates to the literal property name '[object Object]' and does not preserve other properties, and since z.object strips unknown keys by default the sharing-mode parse output contains only access_token — expiry_date/expires_in are silently discarded (O365/Zoom tokens never get a new expiry, causing a refresh + DB write on every calendar operation) and Salesforce's instance_url/id/signature are dropped before prisma.credential.update so the next jsforce.Connection goes to the wrong host

refreshOAuthTokens returns incompatible shapes between modes: in sharing mode it returns a raw fetch Response while callers expect their provider's return type (Google expects gaxios res.data so token.access_token throws TypeError, Hubspot expects a parsed token object so undefined tokens and NaN expiry get persisted, Zoho Bigin/CRM expect axios responses so tokenInfo.data.error throws), and Lark/O365/Webex/Zoom only work if the endpoint mimics each provider's exact response envelope, contradicting the function's documented contract

Zoho Bigin passes the credential ID where a user ID is required: refreshOAuthTokens is called with credentialId instead of credential.userId (unlike every other adapter), so the sync endpoint receives the wrong calcomUserId and the parent app resolves the wrong user or fails

Outbound sync requests carry no authentication: the POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends only calcomUserId and appSlug with no secret or header, while the reverse webhook direction requires CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET, so the parent app cannot distinguish Cal.com from anyone else who can reach an endpoint that hands out live OAuth access tokens for arbitrary user IDs

salesforceTokenSchema requires scope, which Salesforce's refresh-token grant response does not include (scope is only in the initial authorization response), so safeParse always fails, parseRefreshTokenResponse throws, the service constructor rejects, and every Salesforce operation fails in both sharing and non-sharing modes

The refresh_token: 'refresh_token' sentinel is injected unconditionally (including non-sharing mode) whenever parsed data lacks refresh_token: O365's merge of {...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data)} persists the literal string over the user's real refresh token (Zoom persists it via parsedToken.data too), permanently bricking local refresh if sharing is later disabled, the endpoint removed, or an app's schema doesn't re-declare refresh_token

Salesforce now eagerly refreshes tokens and writes to the DB in the constructor path on every service instantiation (every booking/check), hammering the SF token endpoint and hard-failing all Salesforce usage on any transient SF error even when the stored token is valid; the response.statusText !== 'OK' check is unreliable (should be response.ok) since proxies/HTTP2 can strip the reason phrase causing a spurious 400 on HTTP 200, and Salesforce bypasses refreshOAuthTokens entirely so sharing mode still requires locally configured SF app keys

Webhook find-then-create race produces duplicate credentials: findFirst followed by create is not atomic, so two concurrent deliveries (retries, parallel parent instances) both see no credential and both create; once duplicates exist, findFirst (no orderBy) updates an arbitrary one, so syncs can keep updating a stale row while the app reads the other

No response.ok check, timeout, or error handling on the sync fetch in refreshOAuthTokens: if the sync endpoint is down, misconfigured, or returns an error body, callers receive a Response they parse into {}-like objects and failures surface as opaque TypeErrors or the generic 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned', masking the real cause; a hung endpoint stalls booking flows for up to undici's ~300s default timeouts

office365video sends appSlug 'msteams', which doesn't match its app-store slug 'office365video' that the credential-sync webhook validates against prisma.app, so the parent app can't correlate the refresh request with the credential it pushed and the reverse webhook would 404 on msteams

Webhook malformed requests yield unhandled 500s: schema.parse throws an unhandled ZodError, there is no method check (a GET yields a 500 instead of 405/400), and symmetricDecrypt with a mismatched key and JSON.parse of garbage also throw unhandled 500s with no actionable message; additionally the decrypted keys object is persisted with zero shape validation, so a malformed sync silently bricks the app credential with confusing downstream Zod failures

The header name from CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME is not lowercased before lookup: Node lowercases incoming header names, so if the env var contains any uppercase character the lookup always misses and every webhook 403s despite a correct secret
Timing-unsafe comparison of the webhook secret: plain !== is used instead of timingSafeEqual on the only authentication for an endpoint that can overwrite any user's credentials

Error-context regression: O365 previously logged the Zod error and the raw provider response on parse failure, but now every failure across Google/Zoom/O365 throws the context-free 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned', discarding the provider response needed to debug token refresh failures

Google credentials corrupted on every token refresh: parseRefreshTokenResponse() returns the full zod safeParse result ({ success, data }) instead of the parsed data, and the Google Calendar path assigns it directly to credential.key and persists it via prisma.credential.update, so after the first access-token refresh the stored key no longer matches googleCredentialSchema and Google Calendar breaks for every user until they re-auth

Literal placeholder string "refresh_token" is written into stored credentials when the parsed response lacks a refresh_token, permanently overwriting the user's real refresh token (Office365 and Zoom spread tokenResponse.data over existing credentials), bricking the credential if sharing is ever disabled

In sharing mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response but callers expect parsed/axios-style objects: Google reads res?.data (undefined, causing TypeError), Hubspot reads expires_in off it (undefined, persisting NaN/null expiry), and Zoho Bigin/CRM read tokenInfo.data.error (undefined, causing TypeError)

Outbound credential-sync request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries no authentication (no shared secret, no CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET header, no signature), forcing operators to expose an unauthenticated token-dispensing endpoint vulnerable to IDOR/credential disclosure where anyone who can reach it can request any user's access token by ID; at minimum the webhook secret should be attached

Webhook secret in apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts is compared with !== (short-circuiting string comparison) instead of crypto.timingSafeEqual, making the check timing-unsafe despite the secret guarding write-access to every user's app credentials; there is also no rate limiting on the route to slow brute-force attempts

The "minimum token response" schema is effectively a no-op: both computed keys ([z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()]) evaluate to the same string "[object Object]" so the schema reduces to { access_token: z.string() }, and z.object strips unknown keys so the sync-provided expiry is silently discarded from tokenResponse.data (e.g. Office365 never receives a new expiry_date, so its credential is treated as perpetually expired and re-refreshed on every operation)

Zoho Bigin passes credentialId instead of credential.userId as the third argument to refreshOAuthTokens, so in sharing mode the parent app receives a credential ID as calcomUserId and the user lookup fails or matches the wrong entity

Salesforce refreshes tokens unconditionally on every service instantiation with no expiry check, causing a token refresh and DB write per calendar operation plus avoidable Salesforce API-quota consumption; it also bypasses refreshOAuthTokens entirely so credential-sharing mode is silently ignored for Salesforce, inconsistent with every other adapter

Google credentials are corrupted on the first token refresh: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the entire zod safeParse envelope ({success, data}) but Google's CalendarService (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:96-99) assigns it directly into data: {key}, so credential.key becomes {success: true, data: {...}} instead of the flat credential — every consumer reading credential.key.access_token/.refresh_token then fails, breaking Google Calendar for that user until re-auth and effectively losing the stored grant.

Salesforce CalendarService (packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-99): the conn initializer unconditionally POSTs to login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token and updates the credential on every service construction, with no expiry check or caching and bypassing refreshOAuthTokens entirely — since calendar services are constructed per availability check/booking/calendar op, every Salesforce operation gains a serial network round-trip plus a DB write, parallel ops race-write the same credential row, and the Salesforce token endpoint is hit at full request volume (rate-limit/lockout risk).
Salesforce conn initializer hard-fails construction on any refresh error even when the stored access token is still valid, whereas the previous jsforce-based code refreshed lazily on 401.

refreshOAuthTokens (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-15) returns a raw fetch Response in sharing mode, but half the callers expect parsed provider objects: Google CalendarService.ts:93-94 reads res?.data (undefined on a Response, so token.access_token throws TypeError), Zoho Bigin (:91) and Zoho CRM (:204-215) read tokenInfo.data.error (TypeError), and HubSpot (:177-188) is typed as HubspotToken but receives a Response so every field read is undefined and gets persisted into the credential — the sharing feature is broken for these apps on any sharing-enabled deployment.
refreshOAuthTokens performs no response.ok check, so sync-endpoint error pages flow into token parsing.

minimumTokenResponseSchema (parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-11) is broken: the computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] both evaluate to the literal '[object Object]' (Zod schemas don't implement toString; the duplicate key collapses to the second), so the 'minimum' schema validates/keeps only access_token and z.object's default strip discards everything else.

The fallback in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-27 writes the literal string 'refresh_token' into data whenever the parsed result lacks it — always true in sharing mode and whenever an app's own schema omits refresh_token — silently replacing real refresh tokens with a placeholder in persisted credentials; Office365 (which spreads tokenResponse.data straight into the stored credential at office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:252-253) and Zoom's rotated single-use refresh tokens are at risk.

Sharing-mode refresh amplification: because the broken minimum schema strips the expiry the sync endpoint returns, the stored credential's expiry never advances, so apps that refresh when the stored expiry has passed (Office365, Zoom, etc.) refresh on every calendar/video operation — one POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT plus one credential UPDATE per op on the booking hot path.

Zoho Bigin (zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:92) passes the credential ID as the third argument to refreshOAuthTokens, but that parameter is userId (serialized as calcomUserId), so on sharing-enabled deployments the sync endpoint resolves the wrong entity (or another user entirely on ID collision) and stores the wrong user's tokens.

The sync-endpoint fetch in refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-15 has no AbortSignal/timeout and no retry policy, so with sharing enabled a slow or hung customer-configured endpoint stalls booking/availability flows up to undici's default timeouts (minutes).

In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 (refreshAccessToken), the call site stores the full zod safeParse envelope returned by parseRefreshTokenResponse ({ success: true, data: {...} }) directly as the credential's key instead of the parsed data itself, so every persisted Google credential fails googleCredentialSchema.parse on the next load; this breaks Google Calendar in the default configuration on the first token refresh and corrupts stored credentials, requiring re-auth or manual DB surgery

In packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8,10, minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()], which both evaluate to the string "[object Object]" so the second silently overwrites the first; the resulting schema validates almost nothing, and since z.object strips unknown keys by default, every parsed token response in credential-sharing mode is reduced to { access_token }, discarding refresh_token, expiry_date/expires_in, instance_url, etc. before persistence

In packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-27, when parsed data lacks refresh_token a bogus literal string "refresh_token" is injected and then persisted by callers (office365 spreads tokenResponse.data over existing credentials, overwriting the user's real refresh token; Google stores data as the credential key), permanently killing future refresh attempts and forcing re-auth

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts returns the raw fetch Response from CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT in sharing mode but provider-specific objects otherwise, breaking callers written against provider shapes: Google reads res?.data (undefined on a Response) and throws TypeError on token.access_token, Hubspot gets undefined/NaN expiry persisted, Zoho Bigin/CRM expect axios responses so tokenInfo.data is undefined and tokenInfo.data.error throws, and Lark's handleLarkError expects Lark's {code, msg, data} envelope; the any return type hides this mismatch from the compiler

The documented contract for the credential sync endpoint ("response should only contain the access token and expiry date") cannot satisfy the callers: Google needs expiry_date in milliseconds, office365/hubspot need expires_in in seconds, Zoom rotates and returns a new refresh token that must be persisted, and Salesforce needs instance_url

The outbound credential-sync POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-14) sends only calcomUserId and appSlug with no shared secret or signature, while the inbound webhook (app-credential.ts:24-27) requires one; the receiving parent app cannot verify the caller, and since the response carries live access tokens, an exposed endpoint lets anyone request tokens for arbitrary user IDs
In refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-14, response.ok is never checked on the credential-sync response, so a 4xx/5xx (or an HTML error page) is passed downstream and treated as a token payload by callers

packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:~93 passes credentialId (the credential's own id) to the sync endpoint instead of credential.userId as every other call site does, so in sharing mode the parent app receives the wrong identifier as calcomUserId, resolves the wrong user, and returns wrong (or no) tokens that are then persisted to this user's credential

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:~85 checks response.statusText !== "OK" to detect success, but statusText is the HTTP reason phrase (empty for HTTP/2 responses in many clients and not contractual), so a successful refresh can throw a spurious 400 and a failed refresh loses the response body entirely; it should use response.ok / response.status

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:~74-98 now performs an unconditional fetch to login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token plus a credential DB write on every SalesforceCalendarService construction, with no expiry check and regardless of whether credential sharing is enabled, adding a network round-trip and DB write per calendar operation, coupling every Salesforce booking/availability check to the token endpoint's availability, and turning previously-working operations into hard failures when the refresh call fails
The new webhook endpoint apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31 has no req.method check, so the state-mutating endpoint answers GET/PUT as well and a GET probe returns 500 rather than 405

In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:60-62, both appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body) and JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) throw unhandled exceptions on malformed input, so third-party callers integrating against this contract get generic 500s instead of structured 4xx JSON error responses

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-27 compares the shared secret with plain !== instead of a timing-safe comparison (crypto.timingSafeEqual); this is the sole authentication on an endpoint that can overwrite any user's credentials for any app, and a timing oracle (combined with no rate limiting) weakens the only gate

Google Calendar credential key corrupted on every token refresh: parseRefreshTokenResponse() returns the full zod safeParse result ({ success: true, data: {...} }) instead of the parsed data, and Google stores that wrapper directly as the credential key, so googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) fails on next load (fields nested under data), breaking Google Calendar for all users in the default non-sync configuration after the first routine token refresh (~1 hour) until they re-authenticate (CalendarService.ts:96-99)

Sync-mode response shape mismatch crashes multiple apps: in sync mode the raw fetch Response from CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is returned unopened (no response.ok check, body never parsed), but every caller expects a provider-specific shape — googlecalendar reads res?.data (TypeError reading access_token), zoho-bigin and zohocrm read tokenInfo.data.error (TypeError), hubspot assigns the Response to HubspotToken and persists undefined token values, and lark/office365video/webex feed it into handlers expecting the provider's response envelope, so the credential-sync feature is broken on arrival for these apps whenever enabled (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-15 and callers)

minimumTokenResponseSchema computed keys are nonsense: [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] both evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]" (the second overwrites the first), so the intended "any numeric property is the expiry / allow other properties" schema never exists; since zod objects strip unknown keys, sync-mode parsed output contains only access_token — e.g. office365 never receives a new expiry_date, so the credential is perpetually "expired" and the sync endpoint is hit on every calendar operation (parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-11)

Literal "refresh_token" string injected into stored credentials: when the response lacks refresh_token (the documented sync response is only access_token + expiry), the code sets data.refresh_token = "refresh_token" — the literal string — and Office365 then spreads tokenResponse.data over existing credentials and persists it (Zoom likewise), clobbering the real refresh token; if credential sync is later disabled or the endpoint removed, those credentials are permanently broken (parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:24-26)

No timeout, retry, ok-check, or fallback on the sync-endpoint fetch: the new outbound fetch has no AbortController/timeout, no retry, no response.ok handling, and no fallback to the local refreshFunction on failure — when credential sharing is enabled, a hanging parent app stalls bookings indefinitely and a 4xx/5xx is returned raw to callers, with no circuit breaker or health gating for this new runtime dependency in the booking hot path (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-14)

Zoho Bigin passes credential ID as user ID: every other call site passes credential.userId, but this one passes credentialId, which refreshOAuthTokens sends as calcomUserId in the sync request body — in sync mode the parent app receives the credential's DB id as the user id, causing token lookup failure or, worse, tokens fetched for a different user whose id collides and stored under this credential (zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:~91)

Salesforce eager refresh on every instantiation plus fragile status check: a Salesforce token refresh (network call + credential DB write) now runs on every service instantiation where previously jsforce used the stored access token and refreshed lazily, adding a per-operation round trip (a downed/rate-limiting Salesforce now fails operations that previously succeeded with the cached token); the fetch has no timeout, and the guard response.statusText !== "OK" is fragile since HTTP/2 responses carry an empty reason phrase, with the response body discarded on failure so the thrown HttpError says only "Bad Request" with no diagnostic detail (salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:~75-98)

Webhook handler has no error handling: no try/catch anywhere in this externally-reachable handler — schema.parse(req.body) throws ZodError on malformed bodies (unhandled 500 instead of 400, and there is no HTTP method check so a GET with no body 500s), symmetricDecrypt throws on an undecryptable payload or mis-sized key (the || "" fallback only masks misconfiguration), and JSON.parse throws if the decrypted plaintext isn't JSON; unlike other routes, it doesn't use defaultHandler/defaultResponder so the caller can't distinguish its own bad payload from server failure, and nothing is logged for diagnosis (app-credential.ts:31, 57-59)

Webhook create/update race: findFirst → update/create is not atomic, so two concurrent deliveries can both find no credential and both create, leaving duplicate credentials for the same user/app; findFirst without orderBy is then nondeterministic about which duplicate receives updates (app-credential.ts:62-82)

Zod error details discarded: the code replaces the previous detailed failure reporting (office365 logged the zod error and the provider's raw response) with a bare Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned"), dropping the zod error and response body, making provider-side OAuth failures much harder to diagnose in production (parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:19-20)

Webhook secret verification weaknesses: the secret is compared with plain !== (non-constant-time, minor timing side channel), and req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME] is looked up without lowercasing the env value — Node lowercases incoming header names, so a mixed-case CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME silently 403s every valid webhook (app-credential.ts:24-27)

No authentication on the outbound sync request: the request carries only calcomUserId + appSlug in the body — the shared CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is not sent, so anyone who can reach the endpoint can request a user's access tokens; security relies entirely on network isolation of the parent app (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-14)

Decrypted keys stored without schema validation: the decrypted keys are persisted without validating against the target app's credential schema (OAuth callbacks do validate, e.g. googleCredentialSchema), so any JSON value — null, arrays, wrong field names — is stored, and a buggy parent app corrupts credentials that only fail later at booking time with confusing errors (app-credential.ts:57-59, 78)

Google credentials are corrupted on every token refresh: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the whole zod safeParse envelope ({success, data, error}) instead of the parsed data, and CalendarService.ts:97 assigns it directly to key and persists it, permanently bricking the credential for every Google Calendar user on their first token refresh (~1h after connect), regardless of the credential-sharing flag

minimumTokenResponseSchema is broken: computed keys z.string().toString() evaluate to a constant string, so both keys collapse to the same fixed key and the second overwrites the first; zod strips unknown keys by default, so the schema strips expiry_date and all other properties from refreshed credentials, causing tokens to always be treated as expired and refreshed on every call

refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response in sharing mode but callers expect provider-specific shapes: Google reads res?.data (gaxios shape), Zoho reads tokenInfo.data.error, Hubspot expects a token object — all crash or get undefined access tokens; the untyped () => any signature erases type checking at every call site

Placeholder refresh_token = "refresh_token" is injected unconditionally in parseRefreshTokenResponse (not gated on APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED) and, when spread over live credentials and persisted, overwrites real refresh tokens in the DB, unrecoverably bricking credentials if the sync endpoint is ever disabled; a parse function mutating its result with a magic string is also a separation-of-concerns violation

APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is not a boolean: a && b evaluates to the value of b, so the constant is typed string | undefined and holds the raw CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY when enabled, leaking the secret if logged or serialized; it also omits CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT so the real enablement condition is re-implemented and can drift in refreshOAuthTokens.ts and parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts

Salesforce performs an unconditional token refresh and DB write on every service instantiation with no expiry check, adding an extra OAuth round-trip and credential write per booking/operation, duplicating jsforce's own refresh flow (two sources of truth) and bypassing refreshOAuthTokens so credential sharing silently doesn't apply to Salesforce

The outbound credential-sync POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries no authentication header (only calcomUserId/appSlug), so the receiving application cannot verify the request came from its Cal.com instance — asymmetric with the inbound webhook which verifies CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET

The sync endpoint's response-body contract is undefined and matches no caller: Lark's handleLarkError expects Lark's {code, msg, data} envelope, Webex/o365video expect provider JSON, none match 'access token and expiry'; additionally only 4 of ~9 touched apps validate via parseRefreshTokenResponse while the rest pipe the sync response straight through

zoho-bigin passes credentialId where userId is expected in refreshOAuthTokens (the third parameter is sent as calcomUserId to the sync endpoint); every other call site passes credential.userId, so the sync endpoint receives the wrong identity and returns the wrong or no tokens

Dead code: the success check if (!accessTokenParsed.success) in Salesforce can never fire because parseRefreshTokenResponse already throws on !success; same redundancy in O365's ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) — misleads readers about the helper's contract

Hardcoded slug literal /api/integrations/zoho-bigin/callback replaces appConfig.slug in zoho-bigin add.ts for no stated reason while callback.ts still uses appConfig.slug, creating two sources of truth for the same path; relatedly, the nine refreshOAuthTokens call sites each hardcode slug strings with no shared constant, so a typo fails silently against the sync endpoint

Webhook handler app-credential.ts has unvalidated failure modes and no method guard: schema.parse throws a raw ZodError returning 500 instead of 400 for malformed bodies, there is no HTTP method check (GET hits the same path), JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) has no error handling (bad ciphertext/key → opaque 500), and validation, secret check, decryption, and both DB write branches are inlined in one untestable 90-line handler

Diagnostics regression: detailed refresh-failure logging (zodError + provider response) was removed from office365calendar and parseRefreshTokenResponse, so all parse failures across all apps now surface as the same context-free "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned" message with no app slug, zod error, or provider payload, making production debugging of OAuth refresh failures significantly harder

findFirst→create race in the webhook: two concurrent deliveries for the same (userId, appId) can both miss in findFirst and both create (no unique constraint per the 'can't use upsert' comment), producing duplicate credentials

Google Calendar writes the zod safeParse envelope returned by parseRefreshTokenResponse ({ success, data }) directly into credential.key instead of the parsed credentials (googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97), so on the next load googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) throws, the integration is dead, and the user must re-authenticate — this hits every Google Calendar user on first access-token expiry in the default configuration

minimumTokenResponseSchema is structurally broken: z.string().toString() and z.string().optional().toString() both evaluate to '[object Object]', so the object literal has duplicate computed keys that collapse to one garbage key, and the schema silently strips expiry_date/expires_in and refresh_token from every token response while still validating 'green' — expiry is never persisted (perpetual re-refresh for office365/zoom) and the real refresh token never survives parsing (parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-11)

The sync branch of refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response without calling response.json(), but callers expect app-specific token shapes: Google crashes with a TypeError reading token.access_token (Response has no .data), Hubspot and Zoho persist undefined/NaN values into credentials, and Lark's handleLarkError rejects the non-Lark envelope

parseRefreshTokenResponse substitutes the literal string 'refresh_token' when the parsed data lacks a refresh_token, and callers (office365, zoom) persist this placeholder over the user's real refresh token, permanently killing the credential for direct refreshes (parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-27)

Cal.com's outbound request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends only calcomUserId and appSlug with no secret header or signature, so the parent app cannot verify the caller and anyone who can reach the endpoint can harvest fresh OAuth access tokens for arbitrary user IDs
The sync response is never checked with response.ok, so a non-2xx response from the credential sync endpoint is passed downstream and parsed as if it were valid
The outbound sync fetch has no timeout, so a hanging CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT stalls booking flows because the call runs inline in calendar/video service construction

SalesforceCalendarService now performs an eager, unconditional token refresh on every service instantiation with no expiry check (previously jsforce refreshed lazily only on 401), adding a synchronous network round-trip to every Salesforce calendar operation

Any error during the Salesforce token refresh (rate limit, revoked token, missing app keys) throws HttpError 400 in the SalesforceCalendarService constructor, killing operations that previously succeeded with the still-valid cached access token — a cascade from transient upstream conditions to total Salesforce breakage
The response.statusText !== 'OK' check in the Salesforce refresh is fragile because undici returns an empty statusText for HTTP/2 responses, turning successful refreshes into spurious 400 errors

zoho-bigin passes credentialId instead of credential.userId as the calcomUserId argument to refreshOAuthTokens (zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:91), so the sync endpoint looks up the wrong entity (or none) and returns wrong or absent tokens for the user

The webhook secret is compared with a plain !== string comparison (non-constant-time), which is timing-attack-vulnerable for a secret guarding an endpoint that can overwrite any user's app credentials; a constant-time compare such as crypto.timingSafeEqual should be used

The webhook's findFirst → create sequence has a TOCTOU race: two concurrent calls for the same user+app can both miss in findFirst and both create, leaving duplicate credentials because there is no unique constraint on userId+appId
findFirst in the webhook has no deterministic ordering when multiple credential rows already exist, so updates target an arbitrary row

The webhook handler has unhandled throw paths that produce 500s instead of 4xx responses: there is no req.method check (a GET hits zod .parse(undefined)), and malformed bodies, wrong encryption keys, or non-JSON plaintext in symmetricDecrypt/JSON.parse all throw unhandled

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Salesforce conn initializer hard-fails construction on any refresh error even when the stored access token is still valid, whereas the previous jsforce-based code refreshed lazily on 401.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the service now always performs a refresh-token request during initialization (`fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token"...)`) and throws on any non-OK response (`if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw ...`). adjudication_records.issue_text: refreshOAuthTokens (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-15) returns a raw fetch Response in sharing mode, but half the callers expect parsed provider objects: Google CalendarService.ts:93-94 reads res?.data (undefined on a Response, so token.access_token throws TypeError), Zoho Bigin (:91) and Zoho CRM (:204-215) read tokenInfo.data.error (TypeError), and HubSpot (:177-188) is typed as HubspotToken but receives a Response so every field read is undefined and gets persisted into the credential — the sharing feature is broken for these apps on any sharing-enabled deployment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: minimumTokenResponseSchema (parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-11) is broken: the computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] both evaluate to the literal '[object Object]' (Zod schemas don't implement toString; the duplicate key collapses to the second), so the 'minimum' schema validates/keeps only access_token and z.object's default strip discards everything else.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined as `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), [z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional() })`. Those computed property names evaluate to a single concrete string at runtime (whatever `.toString()` returns for the Zod schema objects), not “any key”. This does not create a catch-all schema; instead it defines (at most) one or two fixed keys, and `z.object` will strip all other unknown properties by default. So when the “minimum” path is taken, fields like `expiry_date` (and any other token fields) will be discarded from the parsed output, defeating the intent of accepting/keeping arbitrary token response properties.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The fallback in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-27 writes the literal string 'refresh_token' into data whenever the parsed result lacks it — always true in sharing mode and whenever an app's own schema omits refresh_token — silently replacing real refresh tokens with a placeholder in persisted credentials; Office365 (which spreads tokenResponse.data straight into the stored credential at office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:252-253) and Zoom's rotated single-use refresh tokens are at risk.
matched_golden_ids: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same bug: parseRefreshTokenResponse falls back to writing the literal string 'refresh_token' when the response lacks a refresh_token field, which overwrites/invalidates the real token and can break subsequent refresh/auth flows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Sharing-mode refresh amplification: because the broken minimum schema strips the expiry the sync endpoint returns, the stored credential's expiry never advances, so apps that refresh when the stored expiry has passed (Office365, Zoom, etc.) refresh on every calendar/video operation — one POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT plus one credential UPDATE per op on the booking hot path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a new “minimum token response” path via `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, but the finding’s specific claim (“minimum schema strips the expiry so stored expiry never advances, causing refresh on every operation”) is not verifiable from the shown code. In fact, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined with computed keys like `[z.string().toString()]`, which will not match arbitrary response keys such as `expires_in`/`expiry_date`; this is more likely to make `safeParse` fail and throw (`"Invalid refreshed tokens were returned"`) than to successfully parse while dropping expiry fields. Also, the code paths shown don’t demonstrate the asserted behavior of repeatedly refreshing solely because an expiry was stripped (and some services still manually set expiry fields before parsing).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The sync-endpoint fetch in refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-15 has no AbortSignal/timeout and no retry policy, so with sharing enabled a slow or hung customer-configured endpoint stalls booking/availability flows up to undici's default timeouts (minutes).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts` where, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, it performs a `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams(...) })` with no `AbortSignal`/timeout and no retry/backoff. adjudication_records.issue_text: In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 (refreshAccessToken), the call site stores the full zod safeParse envelope returned by parseRefreshTokenResponse ({ success: true, data: {...} }) directly as the credential's key instead of the parsed data itself, so every persisted Google credential fails googleCredentialSchema.parse on the next load; this breaks Google Calendar in the default configuration on the first token refresh and corrupts stored credentials, requiring re-auth or manual DB surgery

adjudication_records.issue_text: In packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8,10, minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()], which both evaluate to the string "[object Object]" so the second silently overwrites the first; the resulting schema validates almost nothing, and since z.object strips unknown keys by default, every parsed token response in credential-sharing mode is reduced to { access_token }, discarding refresh_token, expiry_date/expires_in, instance_url, etc. before persistence

adjudication_records.issue_text: The documented contract for the credential sync endpoint ("response should only contain the access token and expiry date") cannot satisfy the callers: Google needs expiry_date in milliseconds, office365/hubspot need expires_in in seconds, Zoom rotates and returns a new refresh token that must be persisted, and Salesforce needs instance_url

adjudication.rationale: The new “credential sync endpoint” path is not compatible with several call sites as implemented in this diff. The contract comment in `refreshOAuthTokens` says the endpoint response “should only contain the access token and expiry date”, but callers often rely on provider-specific fields and/or refresh token persistence: (1) Google sets `googleCredentials.expiry_date = token.expiry_date` (expects an `expiry_date` field) and then validates via `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` (which, in sharing mode, only enforces `access_token` + some numeric field, not `expiry_date`), so an endpoint that returns `expires_in` won’t satisfy the code. adjudication_records.issue_text: The outbound credential-sync POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-14) sends only calcomUserId and appSlug with no shared secret or signature, while the inbound webhook (app-credential.ts:24-27) requires one; the receiving parent app cannot verify the caller, and since the response carries live access tokens, an exposed endpoint lets anyone request tokens for arbitrary user IDs

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when credential sync is enabled it POSTs to `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` with only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in the body and no auth material (no shared secret header, signature, etc.). adjudication_records.issue_text: In refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-14, response.ok is never checked on the credential-sync response, so a 4xx/5xx (or an HTML error page) is passed downstream and treated as a token payload by callers

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when credential sync is enabled it does `const response = await fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` and immediately `return response;` with no `response.ok` (or status/content-type) validation. adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts` the new call `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes `credentialId` as the third argument, but `refreshOAuthTokens` treats that argument as `userId` and sends it as `calcomUserId` to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` (`userId.toString()`). Both note this can misclassify successful responses and cause refresh failures/stale credentials.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:~74-98 now performs an unconditional fetch to login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token plus a credential DB write on every SalesforceCalendarService construction, with no expiry check and regardless of whether credential sharing is enabled, adding a network round-trip and DB write per calendar operation, coupling every Salesforce booking/availability check to the token endpoint's availability, and turning previously-working operations into hard failures when the refresh call fails

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, immediately after `const credentialKey = credential.key...`, the code unconditionally calls `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` and then performs `await prisma.credential.update(...)` before returning a `new jsforce.Connection(...)`. Because it throws on non-OK (`if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw ...`) and rejects on parse failure, previously-working calendar operations can now hard-fail whenever the refresh endpoint is unavailable, while also adding a network round-trip + DB write on each time this connection-building path runs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The new webhook endpoint apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31 has no req.method check, so the state-mutating endpoint answers GET/PUT as well and a GET probe returns 500 rather than 405

adjudication_records.issue_text: In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:60-62, both appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body) and JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) throw unhandled exceptions on malformed input, so third-party callers integrating against this contract get generic 500s instead of structured 4xx JSON error responses

Both `zod.parse` and `JSON.parse` will throw on malformed input (and decrypt may also throw), which in a Next.js API handler will surface as an unhandled exception and typically return a generic 500 response rather than a structured 4xx JSON error. adjudication_records.issue_text: Google Calendar credential key corrupted on every token refresh: parseRefreshTokenResponse() returns the full zod safeParse result ({ success: true, data: {...} }) instead of the parsed data, and Google stores that wrapper directly as the credential key, so googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) fails on next load (fields nested under data), breaking Google Calendar for all users in the default non-sync configuration after the first routine token refresh (~1 hour) until they re-authenticate (CalendarService.ts:96-99)

Multiple callers clearly expect a parsed provider/token object (or axios-style response): googlecalendar does `const token = res?.data; googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token` (will be undefined/TypeError with a fetch Response), hubspot assigns the return to `HubspotToken`, zoho-bigin/zohocrm access `.data.error`, and others pass the result into response handlers expecting provider envelopes. adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new logic unconditionally performs a token refresh via `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` and then writes the refreshed token back to Prisma (`prisma.credential.update(...)`) before returning the `jsforce.Connection`, meaning every call to this auth/connection setup now incurs a network round-trip + DB write. Additionally, the failure guard `if (response.statusText !== "OK")` is fragile (it should use `response.ok`/`response.status`), and on failure it discards the response body and throws an `HttpError` with only `statusText` (and a hardcoded `statusCode: 400`), reducing correctness/diagnostic quality. No timeout/abort is used for the `fetch`, so the request can hang indefinitely.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Webhook handler has no error handling: no try/catch anywhere in this externally-reachable handler — schema.parse(req.body) throws ZodError on malformed bodies (unhandled 500 instead of 400, and there is no HTTP method check so a GET with no body 500s), symmetricDecrypt throws on an undecryptable payload or mis-sized key (the || "" fallback only masks misconfiguration), and JSON.parse throws if the decrypted plaintext isn't JSON; unlike other routes, it doesn't use defaultHandler/defaultResponder so the caller can't distinguish its own bad payload from server failure, and nothing is logged for diagnosis (app-credential.ts:31, 57-59)

Webhook create/update race: findFirst → update/create is not atomic, so two concurrent deliveries can both find no credential and both create, leaving duplicate credentials for the same user/app; findFirst without orderBy is then nondeterministic about which duplicate receives updates (app-credential.ts:62-82)

adjudication.rationale: In the new `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler does a non-atomic read-then-write: `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId } })` followed by either `update` or `create`. With concurrent webhook deliveries for the same `(userId, appId)` pair, both requests can observe “no credential” and both proceed to `create`, potentially producing duplicates (or triggering a unique-constraint error if one exists, which is also unhandled). Additionally, `findFirst` has no `orderBy`, so if duplicates exist for any reason, which row gets updated is nondeterministic. This aligns with the finding’s cited lines (~62-82).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Zod error details discarded: the code replaces the previous detailed failure reporting (office365 logged the zod error and the provider's raw response) with a bare Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned"), dropping the zod error and response body, making provider-side OAuth failures much harder to diagnose in production (parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:19-20)

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes Office365’s previous detailed logging on refresh-token parse failure (the `console.error(... tokenResponse.error ... responseJson)` block in `office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`) and replaces validation with `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)`, which on failure throws a generic `Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` without including the Zod error details or provider response body (`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`). This reduces observability/debuggability but does not by itself break OAuth refresh behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Webhook secret verification weaknesses: the secret is compared with plain !== (non-constant-time, minor timing side channel), and req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME] is looked up without lowercasing the env value — Node lowercases incoming header names, so a mixed-case CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME silently 403s every valid webhook (app-credential.ts:24-27)

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler, the secret check uses `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts). Node/Next lowercases incoming header names in `req.headers`, so if `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` is set to any mixed-case value (e.g. `Calcom-Webhook-Secret`), the lookup will miss and valid requests will 403. Also, comparing secrets with plain `!==` is non-constant-time, creating a (minor) timing side-channel for a shared-secret check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No authentication on the outbound sync request: the request carries only calcomUserId + appSlug in the body — the shared CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is not sent, so anyone who can reach the endpoint can request a user's access tokens; security relies entirely on network isolation of the parent app (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-14)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, Cal.com POSTs to the external sync endpoint with only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in the body and no auth headers/secret (no `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, no signature). The diff also introduces `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`/header-name but those are only used for the inbound webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`), not for this outbound sync call, so the parent app has no shared-secret-based way to authenticate the caller beyond network controls. This is a verifiable security defect exposed by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Decrypted keys stored without schema validation: the decrypted keys are persisted without validating against the target app's credential schema (OAuth callbacks do validate, e.g. googleCredentialSchema), so any JSON value — null, arrays, wrong field names — is stored, and a buggy parent app corrupts credentials that only fail later at booking time with confusing errors (app-credential.ts:57-59, 78)

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the decrypted payload is `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` and then persisted directly via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key: keys } })` / `prisma.credential.create({ data: { key: keys, ... } })` without any schema validation tied to the target app’s credential shape. The only validation is that `keys` is a string in the request body schema. So malformed/incorrect JSON (wrong fields/types, arrays/null, etc.) can be stored and only fail later when the credential is used, unlike existing OAuth flows that validate with e.g. `googleCredentialSchema`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Google credentials are corrupted on every token refresh: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the whole zod safeParse envelope ({success, data, error}) instead of the parsed data, and CalendarService.ts:97 assigns it directly to key and persists it, permanently bricking the credential for every Google Calendar user on their first token refresh (~1h after connect), regardless of the credential-sharing flag

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (`{ success, data, error }`), not the parsed data. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the diff changes `const key = googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials);` to `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then persists it via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. That will store the entire safeParse envelope into `credential.key` and corrupt the credential structure. This occurs regardless of the credential-sharing flag because both branches in `parseRefreshTokenResponse` use `safeParse` and return its envelope.

adjudication_records.issue_text: minimumTokenResponseSchema is broken: computed keys z.string().toString() evaluate to a constant string, so both keys collapse to the same fixed key and the second overwrites the first; zod strips unknown keys by default, so the schema strips expiry_date and all other properties from refreshed credentials, causing tokens to always be treated as expired and refreshed on every call

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. Those expressions evaluate immediately to a single constant string (not a dynamic/index-signature), and the second computed property overwrites the first in the object literal. As a result, the schema effectively only validates `access_token` plus (at most) one fixed key, and because Zod object schemas strip unknown keys by default, fields like `expiry_date` (and other provider-specific token fields) will be removed from `refreshTokenResponse.data` when this minimal schema path is used. That makes the finding’s claim (expiry/other properties being stripped due to the broken schema) verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response in sharing mode but callers expect provider-specific shapes: Google reads res?.data (gaxios shape), Zoho reads tokenInfo.data.error, Hubspot expects a token object — all crash or get undefined access tokens; the untyped () => any signature erases type checking at every call site

adjudication.rationale: In sharing mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`), `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the result of `fetch(...)` (a raw `Response`) rather than the provider client’s usual return type (AxiosResponse, GaxiosResponse, HubspotToken, etc.) (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`). Multiple call sites still assume the old shapes: Google Calendar does `const token = res?.data` after `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` (`packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`), which will be `undefined` for a `fetch` Response (no `.data`). Hubspot assigns the return value to `HubspotToken` and later uses token fields (`packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`), which will break if it’s a `Response`. Zoho Bigin uses `tokenInfo.data.error` on the return value (`packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`), which will also break for `Response`. Additionally, the `() => any` typing in `refreshOAuthTokens` erases compile-time checking of these mismatches.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Placeholder refresh_token = "refresh_token" is injected unconditionally in parseRefreshTokenResponse (not gated on APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED) and, when spread over live credentials and persisted, overwrites real refresh tokens in the DB, unrecoverably bricking credentials if the sync endpoint is ever disabled; a parse function mutating its result with a magic string is also a separation-of-concerns violation

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the function always performs `if (!refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token) { refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"; }` with no gating on `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` (only the schema choice is gated). In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the parsed data is spread into the existing credential object: `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) };` and later persisted via `prisma.credential.update(...)`. When the minimum schema is used (sharing enabled + `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`), the upstream response is explicitly expected to omit `refresh_token`, so the parser injects the magic string and the spread overwrites the real stored refresh token with that placeholder, causing irreversible loss of the real refresh token if the sync mode is later disabled. The parser also mutates its parse result, which is a concrete separation-of-concerns issue tied to this behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is not a boolean: a && b evaluates to the value of b, so the constant is typed string | undefined and holds the raw CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY when enabled, leaking the secret if logged or serialized; it also omits CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT so the real enablement condition is re-implemented and can drift in refreshOAuthTokens.ts and parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/constants.ts`, `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is defined as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, which in JS/TS evaluates to the second operand (the raw encryption key string) when enabled, not a boolean. This makes the exported constant type/value `string | undefined` and directly embeds a secret into an exported constant, increasing risk of accidental exposure if it’s ever logged/serialized or bundled. Additionally, actual “syncing” enablement is checked elsewhere as `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` (in `refreshOAuthTokens.ts` / `parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`), while the constant omits the endpoint, duplicating conditions and creating drift risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Salesforce performs an unconditional token refresh and DB write on every service instantiation with no expiry check, adding an extra OAuth round-trip and credential write per booking/operation, duplicating jsforce's own refresh flow (two sources of truth) and bypassing refreshOAuthTokens so credential sharing silently doesn't apply to Salesforce

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the diff adds a token refresh request (`fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token" ...)`) and a `prisma.credential.update(...)` before returning the `jsforce.Connection`, with no conditional/expiry check shown. This makes the refresh+DB write happen whenever this service code path runs. Also, unlike other integrations in this diff, Salesforce does not use the new `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` helper, so when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` + `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, Salesforce refresh will not follow the credential-sync flow. This is a concrete, diff-grounded performance/architecture/feature-consistency issue, but not a strictly provable correctness break from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The outbound credential-sync POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries no authentication header (only calcomUserId/appSlug), so the receiving application cannot verify the request came from its Cal.com instance — asymmetric with the inbound webhook which verifies CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, the credential-sync path does `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams({ calcomUserId, appSlug }) })` with no auth header/signature/secret included. Meanwhile the inbound webhook (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`) explicitly authenticates via `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` in a header. So the finding is accurate: the outbound sync request, as implemented in the diff, provides no built-in way for the receiving app to verify the caller is the Cal.com instance (unless the receiver uses out-of-band controls). This is a concrete, diff-grounded security/integration completeness concern, though it’s presented as “customize payload based on what your endpoint requires,” so it’s more an incomplete design than a provable functional break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The sync endpoint's response-body contract is undefined and matches no caller: Lark's handleLarkError expects Lark's {code, msg, data} envelope, Webex/o365video expect provider JSON, none match 'access token and expiry'; additionally only 4 of ~9 touched apps validate via parseRefreshTokenResponse while the rest pipe the sync response straight through

adjudication.rationale: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns fundamentally different shapes depending on env: when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` it returns a `fetch()` `Response`, otherwise it returns whatever the provider refresh function returns (often an axios-like object / typed token). Several updated callers assume non-`Response` shapes and will break when the sync endpoint is enabled: e.g. Google Calendar does `const token = res?.data` after `refreshOAuthTokens(...)`, but a `Response` has no `.data`; Hubspot expects a `HubspotToken` object directly; Zoho Bigin/Zoho CRM expect `tokenInfo.data...` from axios, but would instead receive a `Response`. Additionally, only some paths use `parseRefreshTokenResponse`; many callers just pass the returned value onward without validating/normalizing, reinforcing that the sync endpoint response contract is not consistently handled across apps.

adjudication_records.issue_text: zoho-bigin passes credentialId where userId is expected in refreshOAuthTokens (the third parameter is sent as calcomUserId to the sync endpoint); every other call site passes credential.userId, so the sync endpoint receives the wrong identity and returns the wrong or no tokens

adjudication.rationale: `refreshOAuthTokens` is defined as `(refreshFunction, appSlug, userId)` and, when syncing is enabled, sends the third argument as `calcomUserId` to `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`). In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the call site passes `credentialId` as the third argument (`refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)`), while other integrations pass `credential.userId`. This would cause the sync endpoint to receive a credential identifier instead of the Cal.com user id, leading to wrong/no refreshed tokens for Zoho Bigin when sync is enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead code: the success check if (!accessTokenParsed.success) in Salesforce can never fire because parseRefreshTokenResponse already throws on !success; same redundancy in O365's ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) — misleads readers about the helper's contract

adjudication.rationale: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws when `safeParse` fails (`if (!refreshTokenResponse.success) { throw new Error(...) }`), so callers will never receive a `{ success: false }` result. In `SalesforceCalendarService`, the subsequent `if (!accessTokenParsed.success)` branch is therefore unreachable/dead code. Similarly, in `Office365CalendarService`, `...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data)` suggests `success` could be false, but this helper guarantees success or throws, making the conditional misleading about the helper’s contract.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hardcoded slug literal /api/integrations/zoho-bigin/callback replaces appConfig.slug in zoho-bigin add.ts for no stated reason while callback.ts still uses appConfig.slug, creating two sources of truth for the same path; relatedly, the nine refreshOAuthTokens call sites each hardcode slug strings with no shared constant, so a typo fails silently against the sync endpoint

Separately, multiple `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "<slug>", ...)` call sites do hardcode slug strings with no shared constant, which is a real, diff-grounded consistency/typo-risk concern but not a demonstrable bug in this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Webhook handler app-credential.ts has unvalidated failure modes and no method guard: schema.parse throws a raw ZodError returning 500 instead of 400 for malformed bodies, there is no HTTP method check (GET hits the same path), JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) has no error handling (bad ciphertext/key → opaque 500), and validation, secret check, decryption, and both DB write branches are inlined in one untestable 90-line handler

adjudication_records.issue_text: Diagnostics regression: detailed refresh-failure logging (zodError + provider response) was removed from office365calendar and parseRefreshTokenResponse, so all parse failures across all apps now surface as the same context-free "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned" message with no app slug, zod error, or provider payload, making production debugging of OAuth refresh failures significantly harder

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes provider-specific refresh failure diagnostics in `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` by deleting the `console.error("Outlook error grabbing new tokens...", tokenResponse.error, ... responseJson)` block and replacing `refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(...)` with `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)`. The new shared helper `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts` throws a generic `Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` on parse failure and does not include the app slug, zod error details, or the provider payload in the error/log output. This makes OAuth refresh failures harder to debug but does not by itself prove broken behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findFirst→create race in the webhook: two concurrent deliveries for the same (userId, appId) can both miss in findFirst and both create (no unique constraint per the 'can't use upsert' comment), producing duplicate credentials

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler does a non-atomic read-then-write: `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId } })` followed by either `credential.update` or `credential.create`. With concurrent webhook deliveries for the same `(userId, appId)`, both requests can observe “no credential” and both attempt `create`, which can produce duplicate credentials (if no DB uniqueness) or trigger a failing create (if there is a unique constraint). The race is directly present in the diff because there’s no transaction/locking or upsert on a unique key.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Google Calendar writes the zod safeParse envelope returned by parseRefreshTokenResponse ({ success, data }) directly into credential.key instead of the parsed credentials (googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97), so on the next load googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) throws, the integration is dead, and the user must re-authenticate — this hits every Google Calendar user on first access-token expiry in the default configuration

adjudication.rationale: In googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts the code now does `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and persists `{ key }` via prisma. But `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (new file packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts) returns the Zod `safeParse` result envelope (`{ success, data, ... }`), not `data` itself. Other call sites (e.g., office365calendar, zoomvideo) treat its return value as an envelope and access `.success`/`.data`. Persisting the envelope into `credential.key` would change the stored shape and can break later code expecting the credential JSON to match `googleCredentialSchema` (i.e., expecting actual credentials fields at the top level).

adjudication_records.issue_text: minimumTokenResponseSchema is structurally broken: z.string().toString() and z.string().optional().toString() both evaluate to '[object Object]', so the object literal has duplicate computed keys that collapse to one garbage key, and the schema silently strips expiry_date/expires_in and refresh_token from every token response while still validating 'green' — expiry is never persisted (perpetual re-refresh for office365/zoom) and the real refresh token never survives parsing (parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-11)
matched_golden_ids: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

It explains these evaluate to `"[object Object]"`, causing a broken Zod object shape (duplicate/garbage keys), which aligns with the golden comment’s point that this is invalid Zod usage and leads to failure/misparsing at runtime.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The sync branch of refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response without calling response.json(), but callers expect app-specific token shapes: Google crashes with a TypeError reading token.access_token (Response has no .data), Hubspot and Zoho persist undefined/NaN values into credentials, and Lark's handleLarkError rejects the non-Lark envelope

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, the sync branch (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`) does `fetch(...)` and returns the raw `Response` object. Multiple callers in the diff expect either an axios-style object with `.data` or a parsed token JSON. For example, Google (`googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`) does `const token = res?.data; googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token;` which will crash because a Fetch `Response` has no `.data`. Similarly, Zoho Bigin (`zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`) expects `tokenInfo.data.error` but would receive a Fetch `Response` in the sync branch, causing incorrect behavior/crash. adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse substitutes the literal string 'refresh_token' when the parsed data lacks a refresh_token, and callers (office365, zoom) persist this placeholder over the user's real refresh token, permanently killing the credential for direct refreshes (parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-27)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, when the parsed token data lacks `refresh_token`, the function mutates the parsed data to set `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` (lines 24-26 in the new file). In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the returned `.data` is spread over the existing `o365AuthCredentials` (`{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }`), so if Microsoft’s refresh response omits `refresh_token`, this placeholder will overwrite the real stored refresh token and then be persisted via `prisma.credential.update`, breaking future direct refreshes. This is a concrete, diff-grounded correctness/data-loss issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cal.com's outbound request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends only calcomUserId and appSlug with no secret header or signature, so the parent app cannot verify the caller and anyone who can reach the endpoint can harvest fresh OAuth access tokens for arbitrary user IDs

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` it performs a `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams({ calcomUserId, appSlug }) })` with no authentication header, signature, or shared secret included. The diff adds webhook-secret verification for the *inbound* `/api/webhook/app-credential` route, but nothing analogous for this *outbound* credential sync call, so the receiving “parent app” has no caller-verification material from Cal.com beyond unauthenticated parameters.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The sync response is never checked with response.ok, so a non-2xx response from the credential sync endpoint is passed downstream and parsed as if it were valid

adjudication.rationale: In the credential-sync path, `refreshOAuthTokens` does a `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` and returns the raw `Response` without checking `response.ok` (or otherwise handling non-2xx) (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`). Callers generally assume a successful token refresh object/response; e.g. Google Calendar does `const token = res?.data` right after calling `refreshOAuthTokens`, which will not be valid for a `fetch` Response and also won’t guard against non-2xx. This makes it possible for a failed sync HTTP response to propagate and be treated as if it contained valid token data (or crash later), rather than being rejected early.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The outbound sync fetch has no timeout, so a hanging CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT stalls booking flows because the call runs inline in calendar/video service construction

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `refreshOAuthTokens` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts) which, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, performs an inline `await fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` with no AbortController/timeout. Multiple integrations now call this helper inside their token refresh paths (e.g., google/office365/zoom/webex CalendarService/VideoApiAdapter), so if that endpoint hangs the awaiting request can block those flows. The specific claim that it occurs during "service construction" isn’t directly shown, but the no-timeout inline await is verifiable and is an operational robustness concern introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SalesforceCalendarService now performs an eager, unconditional token refresh on every service instantiation with no expiry check (previously jsforce refreshed lazily only on 401), adding a synchronous network round-trip to every Salesforce calendar operation

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the service now unconditionally performs a refresh-token HTTP request (`fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token"...)`) immediately after reading `credential.key` and before constructing the `jsforce.Connection`, with no expiry/validity check or conditional gating. This adds an extra network round-trip whenever that code path runs and could have performance/rate-limit implications.
